text:
marta: quick update — canary for v2.3 rollout finished in us-west and us-east, but eu-west p95 is ~120ms higher than baseline, looks like a small drift. asking whether we want to hold + investigate or extend fallback window to avoid user impact.

jake: thanks, what % of traffic is currently routed to the canary in eu-west?

marta: ~10% routed. overall error rates are stable, it's latency only.

kevin: pinged perf dashboard — the spike seems to coincide with a kernel param change on the dedicated hosts at 22:10 UTC. not sure if it's correlated.

lia: can we repro with synthetic load? I can run a short profile against canary hashes if we decide to hold.

marta: repro would be ideal. if we hold, i'd like to run profiling + kv-cache hit-rate check. allocating 30m.

ops-bot: deploy-canary v2.3 started 2024-11-02T21:58:00Z — health: degraded in eu-west (p95 latency +120ms).

sam: proposal: do a 20m hold, run profiles (lia) and a fast bisect stepping down kernel param to previous value (kevin) — if p95 stays high after 20m, rollback. sounds ok? :thinking_face:

kevin: i'll prepare the bisect script. snippet to run on one node: ```for v in 0.1 0.05 0.01; do sudo sysctl -w vm.swappiness=$v; ./run-load.sh --target eu-west --duration 300; done``` won't be perfect but should isolate.

marta: +1 on 20m hold. i'll flip traffic to fallback policy (no increase) while we run tests.

jake: vote: hold + investigate :thumbsup:

lia: starting profile run now against canary-03, will upload flamegraphs to the perf bucket when done.

kevin: starting bisect on host canary-02 now, will post results in ~10m.

ops-bot: canary traffic adjusted: roll-forward paused, fallback window engaged (10% -> 10% fixed).

marta: updating on-call doc: if bisect isolates host-level change, we roll cluster-level revert; if it's model runtime regression, then rollback model. i'll coordinate next steps after results.

sam: if either test is inconclusive by +20m, i recommend rollback to v2.2 to be safe.

kevin: bisect step 1 -> lowered swappiness to 0.05 gave p95 down ~30ms, step 2 -> 0.01 gave additional ~10ms. looks like kernel param strongly affects latency. posting raw numbers in perf channel.

lia: flamegraphs attached (s3://redwood-perf/canary/1778901234/). no obvious runtime hotspot change. kv-cache hit-rate unchanged.

marta: given those results, i propose we proceed with cluster-level revert of the kernel param on dedicated hosts in eu-west, keep canary running, and re-run the canary after hosts stabilize. roll forward is paused.

jake: +1 from infra side, i'll schedule the revert and target a 10m maintenance window.

sam: agreed. revert + re-run canary. thanks everyone.

marta: action items: kevin -> revert kernel param cluster-wide in eu-west; lia -> re-run profile after revert; ops-bot -> keep canary traffic fixed; i'll update the rollout doc and mark canary on hold. will reopen once we see p95 back to baseline.

kevin: starting cluster revert now.

ops-bot: maintenance-window started for eu-west hosts (kernel params revert in progress).

marta: closing loop: after revert p95 in eu-west dropped back to baseline within 5m. canary remains paused for one more smoke run, but no rollback required. i'm unpausing the rollout tomorrow unless new signals show up. :white_check_mark:
